title: finding(pm): `check-issue-citations` prints a remedy arm its own grammar cannot honour — 「keep the number and say in prose」 still fails, because `CITATION_RE` sees the `#`
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 2 (session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`). ⛔ No grading, no routing, no `domain:*` label — an execution seat does none of those. Surfaced independently by **two** `os-dev` agents on two different PRs within an hour, each of which read the script rather than trusting its message.

## The defect

`scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` prints a two-arm remedy when a citation does not resolve:

> Either name a target that resolves, or **keep the number and say IN PROSE that it no longer resolves and what the live record is.**

**Arm two does not work.** Following it literally leaves the gate red.

## Measured on `origin/main`, by reading the grammar rather than the message

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `CITATION_RE` (`:326`) | extracts any `#` + digits out of comment prose; there is no surrounding-context arm that can see an acknowledgement |
| `NON_CITATION_HEADS` (`:337-346`) | **8** entries, and every one is an **ordinal head** — `(prime) directive`, `pd`, `(decision) batch`, `re-charter`, `acceptance`, `clause`, `option`, `§`. ⛔ None recognises prose about a number's liveness |
| a prose / acknowledgement / per-line exemption mechanism anywhere in the script | **none found** |
| the literal string `no longer resolve` in the script | **1** occurrence — and it is inside the printed remedy text, ⛔ not in any matching path |
| LIT CONTROL — `allocated-but-absent` in the same file | **2** occurrences (the classification and its report), so the instrument reads the file and the 1-vs-none split above is a reading |

⇒ If the author keeps the `#`, the number still matches `CITATION_RE`, still classifies `allocated-but-absent`, and the gate still exits 2 — **however true and however prominent the prose beside it**. The only spellings that actually pass are arm one (name a target that resolves) or dropping the `#` sigil.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than learning

Today it cost **two** independent rounds. Both devs converged on the same workaround — keep the digits, drop the leading `#`, e.g. 「issue 14423, written here without a leading hash because it no longer resolves」 — which preserves greppability and passes. That workaround is correct but **undiscoverable from the message**: each one found it only by reading `CITATION_RE` and `NON_CITATION_HEADS` for itself.

⚠️ The cost is about to recur rather than fade. A band of issue numbers was deleted from this board by author (measured: `#8714`/`#8715` 404 with `#8716` 200; `#14918`/`#14919` 404 with `#14920` 200; `#14422`/`#14423` 404 with `#14424` 200 — scattered pairs, each with its lit control built in), so any branch whose prose cites one of them meets this gate on its next push and then meets a remedy that does not work.

## Two shapes a fix could take — ⛔ neither is prescribed here

- **Make the message true**: state that the number must lose its `#` to stop being a citation, and show the passing spelling.
- **Make the grammar match the message**: teach the reader an acknowledgement form (a stated shape beside the number) and add a `--self-test` case pinning it.

⛔ Which one is right is not this seat's call — the first is a one-line honesty fix, the second widens what the gate accepts, and that difference is exactly the kind a gate's owner should decide.

## Not asserted

⛔ The gate is **not** broken at its job: it correctly caught eight dangling citations on one PR and one on another, all independently confirmed 404 against 200 lit controls. ⛔ This card is about the remedy text only.

## Duplicate-search terms

`check-issue-citations` · `allocated-but-absent` · remedy prose · `CITATION_RE` · `NON_CITATION_HEADS`
